title.narrative: International IDEA 2019-2024 Enhancing Women's Political Participation in Africa
International IDEA 2019-2024 Enhancing Women's Political Participation in Africa

description.narrative:
International IDEA har ansökt om 75 miljoner kronor för att finansiera programmet "Enhancing Women's Political Participation in Africa" under perioden 2019-2022. International IDEA kommer att samarbeta med sex panafrikanska organisationer: Gender Links (GL), the African Women’s Development and Communication Network (FEMNET), Women and Law in Southern Africa (WLSA), The Forum for African Women Educationalists (FAWE), Padare och Institut Fondamental d’Afrique Noire (IFAN-Gender Lab) i åtta länder; Botswana, Demokratiska Republiken Kongo, Eswatini, Elfenbenskusten, Kenya, Senegal, Tanzania och Zimbabwe.
Insatsen syftar till att stärka kvinnors politiska deltagande och representation i Afrika genom att 1) stärka policypåverkan, öka medvetenhet om och efterfrågan på inkludering av kvinnor på alla nivåer i beslutsfattande och politiskt deltagande, 2) bygga och stärka plattformar som möjliggör och främjar kvinnors politiska deltagande på alla nivåer, samt 3) bidra till att öka kvinnors röst och påverkan i politiska processer och institutioner i Afrika. Kvinnoorganisationer, andra civilsamhällesaktörer, politiska partier, valmyndigheter, media, parlament, RECs (Regional Economic Communities) och AU (Afrikanska Unionen) är centrala aktörer i programmet.
Insatsens totala budet är 75 miljoner kronor med Sida som enda finansiär. Omkring 52.5 miljoner kronor av budgeten kommer att vidareförmedlas till de sex panafrikanska organisationerna.
I ett första skede tas beslut endast för en första tvåårsfas (med 45 MSEK), detta på grund av otillräckligt utrymme i bemyndiganderamen. Tilläggsbeslut avses tecknas, under förutsättning av medel finns tillgängliga, för det tredje året.

International IDEA has applied for Sida for a funding of 75 Million SEK to carry out a program entitled "Enhancing Women's Political Participation in Africa' to be implemented during the period 2019- 2022. I-IDEA will be collaborating with 6 Pan-African Organizations namely Gender Links (GL), The African Women’s Development and Communication Network (FEMNET), Women and Law in Southern Africa (WLSA), The Forum for African Women Educationalists (FAWE), Padare, The Institut Fondamental d’Afrique Noire (IFAN-Gender Lab) in 8 African Countries (Botswana, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eswatini, Cote d’Ivoire, Kenya, Senegal, Tanzania and Zimbabwe).
The intervention aims increasing the political participation and representation of women in Africa by (1) stepping up advocacy for and expand awareness towards increased demands for the inclusion of women at all levels of political participation and decision-making. (2) building and strengthening enabling platforms that allow for Women’s inclusion in all levels of political participation and (3) contributing towards an increase in the voice and presence of women in political processes and institutions in Africa. Women’s organizations and other civil society groupings, political Parties and election management bodies, the media, parliaments, regional Economic Communities and the African Union are targeted in the project.
The intervention’s total budget is 75 million SEK and Sida is the sole funder of the program. Approximately 52.5 million SEK of the budget will be forwarded to the 6 Pan-African organizations.
At this stage, a decision and agreement will be signed only for the first two years (45 MSEK). This is due to limitations to the framework for outstanding commitments. A supplementary decision is foreseen, if parliamentary appropriations materialize, for the remaining period of the program.

The overarching objective of the intervention is increasing the political participation and representation of women in Africa in line with the Maputo Protocol of 2003, various associated sub-regional protocols and standards, and the SDGs with a view of advancing the goal of gender equality in politics and governance. Specifically the projects intends;
1. To contribute to an increase in the voice and presence of women in political processes and institutions in Africa.
2. To step up advocacy for and expand awareness towards increased demands for the inclusion of women at all levels of political participation and decision-making.
3. Through building the capacity of local and national womens organizations, groupings, networks, mobilisers, community activists, elected female office holders, and others to engage, negotiate, forge alliances, to create enabling platforms that allow for womens inclusion in all levels of political participation.
4. To improve the attitude of political parties, parliaments, and the media to build constituencies, alliances, norms, templates, and targets so that they have positive contributions towards greater womens political participation.
5. To enhance knowledge sharing through research to serve the goals of policy and political reform, capacity enhancement and advocacy that will be pursued.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
The Enhancing Women's Political Participation (WPP) Project was implemented by International IDEA with six consortium members in 8 African countries during five years (2019 2024). The project has contributed to an increase of women involvement in politics.
Strategically WPP contributed to the transformation of womens political participation from isolated aspiration in various countries into an organized, evidence-informed regional movement for inclusive governance.
Despite the slowest annual increase of women's representation in election since 2017, WPP contributed to the successful election of more than 80 women to national and local governance positions.
WPP contributed to an exemplary shift in the internal structures of political parties including the establishment of womens wings in five major parties in Côte dIvoire and the adoption of voluntary quotas in Botswana.
WPP influenced legislative reform engaging electoral commissions and parliamentary institutions which contributed to 42% representation of women in the Constitutional Review Commission in Botswana and development of gender-sensitive electoral frameworks and institutional action plans in Tanzania and Zimbabwe.
At the regional level, WPP contributed to elevation of womens participation in the continental governance agenda through strategic convenings with the African Union, SADC, ECOWAS, and EAC. For instance, the adoption of the Pan-African Model Gendered Electoral Law which was developed by WLSA and its consideration by regional bodies including SADC PF, underscored WPPs growing influence in shaping harmonized legal standards for womens political inclusion.
The Africa WPP Barometer, published in 2021 and updated in 2024, provided cutting-edge data and analysis that informed country-level policy reforms and continental advocacy efforts.
The programme also contributed to results in the realm of public discourse and media engagement. Through the #WomenLeadAfrica campaign and other multi-channel media strategies, WPP reached an estimated 3.2 million people across digital and traditional platforms, amplifying the visibility and legitimacy of women political leaders.
The relevance of the WPP project is indisputable as it confronted the deep-rooted and systemic barriers that have historically limited womens participation in politics and representation across Africa. These barriers are embedded in cultural beliefs, social practices, and even legal frameworks.
Importantly, the WPPs focus on empowering women to participate in political spaces and address persistent inequalities in political participation and representation is not only a matter of justice but also a fundamental aspect of inclusive and sustainable development.
